sourceShortSummaries: The party inventories the fort's relics, leaves the petrified Arcus behind, and makes the three-day journey west to a crowded Karawa.
sourceLongSummaries: Waking in the now-peaceful temple, the party confirms that the tunnel beneath the fort was dug by a creature and predates the recent disturbances. They inventory the relics recovered from the temple and caverns, copy the Black Iron Staff's Draconic inscription, and debate what to do about the cockatrices and the petrified explorer. Seeker sketches Arcus before the party leaves him in the fort and carries the relics west across the desert. The unnatural tension has lifted from the land, and after three days of uneventful travel they reach Karawa, where crowds have gathered for the Festival of Rebirth.

sourceShortSummaries: The party reports its success to Kisa, who connects current dangers to the Summer of Red Storms and directs them to Ikram and Candrosa.
At the caravanserai, Ikram identifies the petrified explorer as Arcus and shares news about his movements, recent attacks, and the coming festival.
sourceLongSummaries: The party finds Kisa in Karawa's council chamber and reports that it destroyed the apparent source of the animals' unnatural aggression. Kisa says the last three days have been quiet but that returning travelers report fresh axebeak attacks. The Draconic inscription on the Black Iron Staff leaves her out of her depth, and she recommends consulting Candrosa. She recounts the Summer of Red Storms, when half-human, half-hyena creatures crossed the border about forty years ago, and identifies Seeker's sketch as a stranger rather than a Karawa local. She directs the party to Ikram for more information and offers them food and lodging at the town's expense.

Ikram welcomes the party to his crowded caravanserai and recognizes Seeker's sketch as Arcus, a quiet foreign traveler who stayed one night four or five weeks earlier. Arcus paid with old Chardonian silver, showed a strong interest in artifacts, and spoke with the smith Jasu before leaving. Ikram also describes attacks on Akan's and Devana's families, discusses the festival's axebeak-riding competition, and explains that cockatrice petrification is normally temporary. He recommends Alesh for ancient artifacts and Candrosa for magic before the party decides to question Jasu.

sourceShortSummaries: After comparing maps and theories about Arcus, the party learns from Jasu that the explorer left behind strangely resilient silvered spearpoints.
At the Charmhearts' camp, a disheveled Ander points at Wellby and speaks blissfully of a master who will consume him and the world.
sourceLongSummaries: The party compares Wellby's map with Seeker's observations of ley lines and considers possible links among Arcus, Chardon, and the recent disturbances. They find Jasu closing his blacksmith shop and accompany him back to Ikram's, where he recognizes Arcus from Seeker's sketch. Jasu says Arcus was interested in Great War artifacts and left two silvered spearpoints to be hafted, expecting to return within weeks. The metal resists heat, reforging, and every attempt to work it, so Jasu promises to show the spearpoints to the party in the morning. He also names Alesh as the best local expert on Dunmari artifacts.

The party walks through Karawa's festival encampment to the colorful wagons of a large Sembaran halfling company. Bree Charmheart welcomes them at first, but grows guarded when Wellby asks about an ill and disheveled companion who had spoken into his mind. As the party prepares to leave, Ander Charmheart staggers from a wagon, points at Wellby, says that he spoke to him, and declares with serene joy that the master will eat him soon. Once they are away, Wellby explains that Ander hears an endless voice promising joy, demanding that he join the master, and saying the master will consume the world. The party suspects a connection to the Black Iron Staff and the disturbances around Karawa.

sourceShortSummaries: Candrosa interrupts the party's vigil at the oasis and insists on speaking after Wellby retrieves a very drunk Kenzo from Ikram's.
Candrosa reveals that Shakun's ancient border protections are failing and asks the party to help defend Dunmar from threats now crossing its borders.
sourceLongSummaries: Delwath, Seeker, and Wellby settle near Karawa's oasis for an overnight vigil, hoping that meditation might bring insight from Shakun, while Kenzo continues drinking with Ikram. Around 10:30 or 11:00 p.m., Candrosa crosses the temple plaza, interrupts the vigil, and says that new messages make an immediate conversation necessary. He sends Wellby to collect Kenzo, whose attempted halfling sobering ritual with three eggs and a stick ends in thrown eggs. As the party gathers, a young, well-equipped warrior later identified as Havdar rides from the Temple of Shakun toward the encampment.

Candrosa leads the party into a side room of the Temple of Shakun, where the Black Iron Staff and their questions expose his fear and uncertainty. After hearing why each traveler came to Karawa, he casts Zone of Truth and asks whether they intend to aid the town. Satisfied, he reveals that Shakun's magic has hidden and protected Dunmar's borders since the aftermath of the Great War, but now seems to have failed. Havdar has returned from fighting half-human, half-hyena creatures south of Karawa, an unending lightning storm has appeared to the northeast, and Ander's voice adds another unexplained threat. Candrosa begs the party to serve as the mundane defense Shakun no longer provides, asks for secrecy to prevent panic before the Festival of Rebirth, and proposes speaking with Havdar in the morning. Before sending them to rest, he gives each traveler a vial of healing mud as thanks and a token of trust.

recapBlocks.title: Following Arcus's Trail
sourceShortSummaries: The party reports its success to Kisa, who connects current dangers to the Summer of Red Storms and directs them to Ikram and Candrosa.
At the caravanserai, Ikram identifies the petrified explorer as Arcus and shares news about his movements, recent attacks, and the coming festival.
After comparing maps and theories about Arcus, the party learns from Jasu that the explorer left behind strangely resilient silvered spearpoints.
sourceLongSummaries: The party finds Kisa in Karawa's council chamber and reports that it destroyed the apparent source of the animals' unnatural aggression. Kisa says the last three days have been quiet but that returning travelers report fresh axebeak attacks. The Draconic inscription on the Black Iron Staff leaves her out of her depth, and she recommends consulting Candrosa. She recounts the Summer of Red Storms, when half-human, half-hyena creatures crossed the border about forty years ago, and identifies Seeker's sketch as a stranger rather than a Karawa local. She directs the party to Ikram for more information and offers them food and lodging at the town's expense.

Ikram welcomes the party to his crowded caravanserai and recognizes Seeker's sketch as Arcus, a quiet foreign traveler who stayed one night four or five weeks earlier. Arcus paid with old Chardonian silver, showed a strong interest in artifacts, and spoke with the smith Jasu before leaving. Ikram also describes attacks on Akan's and Devana's families, discusses the festival's axebeak-riding competition, and explains that cockatrice petrification is normally temporary. He recommends Alesh for ancient artifacts and Candrosa for magic before the party decides to question Jasu.

The party compares Wellby's map with Seeker's observations of ley lines and considers possible links among Arcus, Chardon, and the recent disturbances. They find Jasu closing his blacksmith shop and accompany him back to Ikram's, where he recognizes Arcus from Seeker's sketch. Jasu says Arcus was interested in Great War artifacts and left two silvered spearpoints to be hafted, expecting to return within weeks. The metal resists heat, reforging, and every attempt to work it, so Jasu promises to show the spearpoints to the party in the morning. He also names Alesh as the best local expert on Dunmari artifacts.

recapBlocks.title: The Voice among the Charmhearts
sourceShortSummaries: At the Charmhearts' camp, a disheveled Ander points at Wellby and speaks blissfully of a master who will consume him and the world.
sourceLongSummaries: The party walks through Karawa's festival encampment to the colorful wagons of a large Sembaran halfling company. Bree Charmheart welcomes them at first, but grows guarded when Wellby asks about an ill and disheveled companion who had spoken into his mind. As the party prepares to leave, Ander Charmheart staggers from a wagon, points at Wellby, says that he spoke to him, and declares with serene joy that the master will eat him soon. Once they are away, Wellby explains that Ander hears an endless voice promising joy, demanding that he join the master, and saying the master will consume the world. The party suspects a connection to the Black Iron Staff and the disturbances around Karawa.

recapBlocks.title: Shakun's Failing Protection
sourceShortSummaries: Candrosa interrupts the party's vigil at the oasis and insists on speaking after Wellby retrieves a very drunk Kenzo from Ikram's.
Candrosa reveals that Shakun's ancient border protections are failing and asks the party to help defend Dunmar from threats now crossing its borders.
sourceLongSummaries: Delwath, Seeker, and Wellby settle near Karawa's oasis for an overnight vigil, hoping that meditation might bring insight from Shakun, while Kenzo continues drinking with Ikram. Around 10:30 or 11:00 p.m., Candrosa crosses the temple plaza, interrupts the vigil, and says that new messages make an immediate conversation necessary. He sends Wellby to collect Kenzo, whose attempted halfling sobering ritual with three eggs and a stick ends in thrown eggs. As the party gathers, a young, well-equipped warrior later identified as Havdar rides from the Temple of Shakun toward the encampment.

Candrosa leads the party into a side room of the Temple of Shakun, where the Black Iron Staff and their questions expose his fear and uncertainty. After hearing why each traveler came to Karawa, he casts Zone of Truth and asks whether they intend to aid the town. Satisfied, he reveals that Shakun's magic has hidden and protected Dunmar's borders since the aftermath of the Great War, but now seems to have failed. Havdar has returned from fighting half-human, half-hyena creatures south of Karawa, an unending lightning storm has appeared to the northeast, and Ander's voice adds another unexplained threat. Candrosa begs the party to serve as the mundane defense Shakun no longer provides, asks for secrecy to prevent panic before the Festival of Rebirth, and proposes speaking with Havdar in the morning. Before sending them to rest, he gives each traveler a vial of healing mud as thanks and a token of trust.
